en.one: The leader in pharmacy software in France (market share about 40%). It passed the moat test, but its returns are falling and it failed the test of retained earnings.
en.business: Equasens (formerly Pharmagest) sells management software, hardware and maintenance to pharmacies, nursing homes, hospitals and doctors. 2025 revenue was 236.5 million euros, of which 172.2 million came from the pharmacy division (Pharmagest). France brings 87.5% of revenue. Maintenance and subscription revenue was 105.1 million euros, about 44% of revenue (our calculation); the rest is hardware, installation and new sales.
en.moat_text: The moat is narrow. The company leads pharmacy software in France: its share is about 40%, unchanged from a year earlier; its rivals are Everys and Smart-Rx (Cegedim). Its nursing-home software is used by about 2,650 facilities in France and about 950 in Belgium. Changing pharmacy software is a burden, so customers do not leave easily. Operating margin was 20.4% in 2025 and 19.0% in the first half of 2026. The weak side: returns are falling. Real return on equity was 22.8% in 2021, 14.6% in 2024, 15.4% in 2025 and 13.3% for the last 12 months. Outside France the company is small: about 5% share in Italy, 2% in Germany. The number of pharmacies in France is shrinking (19,676 at the end of 2024; about 300 closures in 2025). Part of revenue depends on the state's digital health programme (Ségur); it lifted profit in 2022-2023, and profit then fell. We looked for gross margin in the inflation years; it is not in the documents read.
en.mgmt: The controlling shareholder is the pharmacists' cooperative group Welcoop: Marque Verte Santé holds more than half of the capital and La Coopérative Welcoop 5-10%. The company has net cash: 93.2 million euros on 30 June 2026. The dividend for 2025 is 1.40 euros per share (1.25 for 2024 and 2023); about half of profit is paid out. The other half stays in the company and goes to acquisitions (24.1 million euros of financial investments in 2025, funded by bank loans; 80% of Erevo, Novaprove, DIS). Even so, real profit fell over five years: the test of retained earnings was failed, which is why D is 1. Goodwill is 128.0 million euros, 51% of parent equity. Buybacks are only under the liquidity contract (bought and sold at about 42.2 euros on average in 2025). Share-based pay is negligible (45,000 options granted in 2020). One-off charges: none in the documents read. A 2.0 million euro provision was booked for a tax reassessment on 2021 (IP Box); the company is contesting it. The chairman of the board changed in June 2026. We looked for pension and off-balance-sheet obligations; they are not in the documents read.
en.latest: 29 October 2026: The company reported third-quarter revenue of 57.3 million euros, +2.0%; −0.2% excluding acquisitions. Nine-month revenue was 181.8 million euros (+5.6%; +0.9% excluding acquisitions). The pharmacy division grew 3.1% over nine months; E-Connect fell 23.4%. On 21 September 2026 there was an incident at the head office and storage facility; the company said it had no impact on third-quarter business. First-half results published on 28 September 2026: revenue 124.5 million euros (+7.3%; +1.4% excluding acquisitions), net profit attributable to the group 19.0 million euros (17.3 million a year earlier), earnings per share 1.26 euros (1.15).
risks: The test of retained earnings was failed: about half of profit stays in the company and goes to acquisitions, yet real profit fell over five years. Real return on equity dropped from 22.8% to 13.3%; the calculation therefore assumes profit keeps shrinking.
Growth comes from acquisitions: excluding them, growth was 0.9% in the first nine months of 2026 and −0.2% in the third quarter.
Revenue is sensitive to the timetable of a public programme: the second wave of Ségur runs until the first half of 2027; when it ends, hardware and installation sales may fall again.
The number of pharmacies in France falls every year; the company has to hold its share in a shrinking customer base.
Goodwill is about half of parent equity (128.0 million euros); if acquired businesses do not deliver the expected profit, impairments will follow.

ALSEM.one: Çip üretim makineleri için elektrostatik tutucu yapan küçük bir Fransız şirketi. Marjları yüksek, hendek ölçütünü geçti; ama borsa geçmişi kısa ve işi çip döngüsüne bağlı.
ALSEM.business: SEMCO Technologies, çip üretiminde silikon plakayı makinenin içinde sabit tutan elektrostatik tutucuları (eChuck) tasarlar ve Montpellier'de üretir. Müşterileri çip üretim makinesi yapan uluslararası şirketlerdir; parça her müşteri için özel tasarlanır. 2025'te hasılat 34,2 milyon avro, net kâr 10,1 milyon avro. 2026 başında 17 müşteri seri üretimdeydi (2025'te 15); 6 müşteri prototip, 10 müşteri onay aşamasındaydı.
ALSEM.moat_text: Hendek dar. Kanıt marjlarda: brüt marj 2024'te %65,3, 2025'te %66,3, 2026'nın ilk yarısında %67,6; faaliyet marjı %36,8, %40,7 ve %40,7. Parça müşterinin makinesi için özel tasarlanır ve seri üretime girmeden önce uzun bir onay sürecinden geçer; onaylanan parçayı değiştirmek müşteri için pahalıdır. Reel özsermaye kârlılığı 2024'te %39,8, 2025'te %54,9. Zayıf yanları: şirket pazar payını ve en büyük müşterilerinin hasılattaki payını açıklamıyor; rakipler arasında çok daha büyük, genel üreticiler var. Şirket küçük (hasılat 34 milyon avro) ve tek üretim yerine bağlı. Kaynaktaki beş yıllık veri eksik (2020-2022 yok), brüt marjın 2022-2023 enflasyon yıllarındaki seyri okunan belgelerde yok. Bu yüzden hendek geniş sayılmadı.
ALSEM.mgmt: Hâkim ortak ECM Group: halka arzdan sonra ECM Technologies sermayenin %70,0'ını tutuyor; halka açık pay yaklaşık %30. ECM Group aile şirketidir. Şirket Temmuz 2025'te hisse başına 15 avrodan Euronext Growth'ta halka açıldı; 46,2 milyon avroluk arzın yaklaşık 42 milyonu ana ortağın sattığı paylardı, şirkete yalnız yaklaşık 4 milyon avro girdi. Halka arzdan önce ana ortağa 6,0 milyon avro temettü ödendi; 2024'te Çin'deki bağlı ortaklığın payları ECM Group'un başka bir şirketine satıldı. Bu ilişkili taraf işlemleri yüzünden D puanı 1. 2025 kârının %45'inin temettü olarak dağıtılması önerildi; 2028 hedefi en az %30. Kaynaktaki %927'lik pay artışı uyarısı halka arz öncesi pay yapısındaki değişimden kaynaklanıyor; halka arzda çıkarılan yeni pay 266.666 (yaklaşık %2,7). 30 Haziran 2026'da nakit 12,3 milyon avro, finansal borç 3,4 milyon avro. Kâr kapasite artışına gidiyor: 2028'e kadar üretim kapasitesinin üç katına çıkarılması planlanıyor. Hisse bazlı ücret, şerefiye, emeklilik ve bilanço dışı yükümlülüklere bakıldı; okunan belgelerde yok (yalnız sonuç açıklamaları okunabildi).
ALSEM.latest: 22 Eylül 2026: Yönetim kurulu ilk yarı sonuçlarını onayladı. Hasılat 19,9 milyon avro (+%19,6), brüt marj %67,6, faaliyet kârı 8,1 milyon avro (marj %40,7), net kâr 5,8 milyon avro (geçen yıl 4,1 milyon; +%39,3). risks: Çip üretim makinesi yatırımları döngüseldir; şirketin elimizdeki verisi yalnız yükseliş yıllarını gösteriyor. Döngü dönerse siparişler ve %40'lık marj birlikte düşebilir.
Müşteri yoğunlaşması bilinmiyor: şirket en büyük müşterilerinin payını açıklamıyor; seri üretimdeki müşteri sayısı yalnız 17.

Üretim tek yerde (Montpellier) ve kapasite üç katına çıkarılıyor; yatırım gecikirse ya da talep gelmezse sermaye getirisi düşer.

en.one: A small French maker of electrostatic chucks for chip-making machines. Margins are high and it passed the moat test, but its listed history is short and the business follows the chip cycle.
en.business: SEMCO Technologies designs electrostatic chucks (eChucks), the parts that hold the silicon wafer in place inside a chip-making machine, and makes them in Montpellier. Its customers are international makers of chip production equipment; each part is designed for the customer. In 2025 revenue was 34.2 million euros and net profit 10.1 million euros. At the start of 2026, 17 customers were in serial production (15 in 2025), 6 in prototyping and 10 in qualification.
en.moat_text: The moat is narrow. The evidence is in the margins: gross margin was 65.3% in 2024, 66.3% in 2025 and 67.6% in the first half of 2026; operating margin 36.8%, 40.7% and 40.7%. The part is designed for the customer's machine and goes through a long qualification before serial production; replacing a qualified part is costly for the customer. Real return on equity was 39.8% in 2024 and 54.9% in 2025. The weak sides: the company does not disclose its market share or how much of revenue its largest customers bring; its rivals include much larger, generalist manufacturers. It is small (revenue of 34 million euros) and depends on one production site. The five-year data in the source is incomplete (2020-2022 are missing), and gross margin for the inflation years 2022-2023 is not in the documents read. So the moat was not classed as wide.
en.mgmt: The controlling shareholder is ECM Group: after the IPO, ECM Technologies holds 70.0% of the capital; the free float is about 30%. ECM Group is family-owned. The company listed on Euronext Growth in July 2025 at 15 euros a share; about 42 million of the 46.2 million euro offering was shares sold by the parent, and only about 4 million euros went to the company. Before the IPO a 6.0 million euro dividend was paid to the parent; in 2024 the shares of the Chinese subsidiary were sold to another ECM Group company. Because of these related-party dealings, D is 1. A dividend of 45% of 2025 profit was proposed; the 2028 target is at least 30%. The 927% share-count warning in the source comes from the change in share structure before the IPO; the new shares issued in the IPO were 266,666 (about 2.7%). On 30 June 2026 cash was 12.3 million euros and financial debt 3.4 million euros. Profit goes into capacity: production capacity is to be tripled by 2028. We looked for share-based pay, goodwill, pension and off-balance-sheet obligations; they are not in the documents read (only the results releases could be read).
en.latest: 22 September 2026: The board approved the first-half results. Revenue was 19.9 million euros (+19.6%), gross margin 67.6%, operating profit 8.1 million euros (margin 40.7%), net profit 5.8 million euros (4.1 million a year earlier; +39.3%). Extraordinary items were a 0.2 million euro expense (a 0.3 million euro gain a year earlier). Equity was 24.7 million euros. The company repeated the 2028 targets given at its IPO: revenue above 55 million euros and an operating margin above 40%. 2025 results published on 13 April 2026: revenue 34.2 million euros, net profit 10.1 million euros (+46.2%).
risks: Spending on chip-making equipment is cyclical; the data we have for the company shows only the upswing. If the cycle turns, orders and the 40% margin may fall together.
Customer concentration is unknown: the company does not disclose the share of its largest customers; only 17 customers are in serial production.
The listed history is short (July 2025) and the five-year data in the source is incomplete; long-run profitability cannot be tested with the figures here.
The parent, ECM Group, holds 70% of the capital; there was an intra-group sale and a large dividend to the parent in the past.
Production is at one site (Montpellier) and capacity is being tripled; if the investment is delayed or demand does not come, the return on capital falls.

SWP.one: Kamu kurumlarına ve enerji şirketlerine bilişim hizmeti ve yazılım satar. Hızlı büyüyor; ama hendek zayıf olduğu için 3. suru geçemedi.
SWP.business: Sword Group, merkezi Lüksemburg'da olan bir bilişim hizmetleri şirketidir: yazılım geliştirme, veri ve yapay zekâ projeleri, kurumsal sistemlerin işletimi. 2026'nın ilk yarısında hasılat 187,7 milyon avro: İsviçre 73,1, Birleşik Krallık 59,5, Belçika-Lüksemburg 46,7, İspanya 8,4 milyon avro. Müşteri grupları: enerji şirketleri 49,2, Avrupa kurumları 45,4, hükümetler 44,1 milyon avro. 2025 sonunda 3.610 çalışanı vardı. FAVÖK marjı %12.
SWP.moat_text: Hendek zayıf; şirket bu yüzden 3. suru geçemedi (B = 1). İş, insan gücüne dayalı bilişim hizmetidir ve büyük bölümü kamu kurumlarından alınan sözleşmelere dayanır; bu işler çoğunlukla ihale ve çerçeve sözleşmeyle kazanılır. Üstünlüğü var: 23,2 aylık sipariş birikimi (30 Haziran 2026), 1.000'den fazla müşteri, uzun süreli kamu ilişkileri. Ama fiyatlama gücünün kanıtı yok: FAVÖK marjı yıllardır %12 dolayında sabit ve şirketin hedefi de bu. Reel özsermaye kârlılığı son 12 ayda %27,2; bu yüksekliğin bir nedeni özsermayenin küçülmesi (30 Haziran 2026'da 68,5 milyon avro; 2024 sonunda toplam 97,1 milyon). 2022'deki %100,3 olağan bir yılı göstermez: kaynakta o yılın F/K'sı 3,4; nedeni bu çalıştırmada belgeden okunmadı.
SWP.mgmt: En büyük ortaklar Eximium (%20,0) ve kurucu Jacques Mottard'ın şirketi Financière Sémaphore (%17,9); halka açık pay %59,7 (31 Aralık 2025). Şirket kârının neredeyse tamamını dağıtıyor: hisse başına 2,00 avro temettü (toplam 18,9 milyon avro; 2025 ana ortaklık kârı 19,0 milyon avro). Satın almalar ve bağlı ortaklık yöneticilerinin paylarının geri alınması borçla karşılanıyor: finansal borç 124,8 milyon avro, şirketin açıkladığı net borç 60,5 milyon avro (2025 sonunda 28,2 milyon). Yöneticilerin ortak yatırım fonuna karşı geri alım yükümlülüğü 28,7 milyon avro. Yinelenen 'tek seferlik' giderler var: 2024'te 5,6 milyon, 2025'te 8,9 milyon, 2026'nın ilk yarısında 4,3 milyon avro (satın alma, işten çıkarma, yeniden yapılanma); bunları olağan gider saydık. Şerefiye 96,3 milyon avro, özsermayenin 1,4 katı. Emeklilik karşılığı 0,3 milyon avro; bilanço dışı garantiler 0,25 milyon avro. Hisse opsiyonu planı yok.
SWP.latest: 22 Ekim 2026: Şirket üçüncü çeyrek sonuçlarını açıkladı: hasılat 100,2 milyon avro (organik büyüme %16,6), FAVÖK 12,0 milyon avro (marj %12,0). Dokuz ayda hasılat 287,9 milyon avro, FAVÖK 34,5 milyon avro. 2026 hedefleri korundu. İlk yarı (rapor 31 Temmuz 2026): hasılat 187,7 milyon avro (+%6,8; organik +%12,6), ana ortaklık net kârı 11,2 milyon avro (geçen yıl 8,8 milyon), hisse başına kâr 1,18 avro (0,94). Kârın içinde, azınlık paylarını geri alma yükümlülüğünün yeniden değerlemesinden gelen 2,2 milyon avro finansman geliri var.
risks: Borç artıyor: şirketin açıkladığı net borç altı ayda 28,2 milyon avrodan 60,5 milyon avroya çıktı; kârın tamamına yakını temettü olarak dağıtılırken satın almalar borçla yapılıyor.
Hasılatın yaklaşık dörtte biri Avrupa kurumlarından geliyor (2026 ilk yarı: %24; bizim hesabımız); bu iş ihalelere bağlı ve ilk yarıda 51,9 milyon avrodan 45,4 milyon avroya geriledi.
Şirket Lüksemburg merkezli; işinin çoğu İsviçre ve Birleşik Krallık'ta. Buradaki enflasyon düzeltmesi Fransa enflasyonuyla yapıldı; frank ve sterlin kuru avro cinsinden kârı etkiler.

en.one: Sells IT services and software to public bodies and energy companies. It is growing fast, but it did not pass the third wall because its moat is weak.
en.business: Sword Group is an IT services company based in Luxembourg: software development, data and artificial intelligence projects, running enterprise systems. Revenue in the first half of 2026 was 187.7 million euros: Switzerland 73.1, the United Kingdom 59.5, Belgium-Luxembourg 46.7 and Spain 8.4 million euros. Customer groups: energy companies 49.2, European institutions 45.4, governments 44.1 million euros. It had 3,610 employees at the end of 2025. The EBITDA margin is 12%.
en.moat_text: The moat is weak; this is why the company did not pass the third wall (B = 1). The business is people-based IT services, and much of it rests on contracts from public bodies, which are mostly won through tenders and framework contracts. It has advantages: a backlog of 23.2 months (30 June 2026), more than 1,000 customers and long public-sector relationships. But there is no evidence of pricing power: the EBITDA margin has been flat at around 12% for years, and that is also the company's target. Real return on equity is 27.2% for the last 12 months; one reason it is high is that equity has shrunk (68.5 million euros on 30 June 2026; total equity was 97.1 million at the end of 2024). The 100.3% of 2022 is not an ordinary year: the source shows a P/E of 3.4 for that year; the reason was not read from a document in this run.
en.mgmt: The largest shareholders are Eximium (20.0%) and Financière Sémaphore, the company of founder Jacques Mottard (17.9%); the free float is 59.7% (31 December 2025). The company pays out nearly all of its profit: a dividend of 2.00 euros per share (18.9 million euros in total; 2025 profit attributable to the group was 19.0 million euros). Acquisitions and the buyback of subsidiary managers' stakes are funded with debt: financial debt is 124.8 million euros and net debt as reported by the company 60.5 million euros (28.2 million at the end of 2025). The buyback commitment to the managers' co-investment fund is 28.7 million euros. There are recurring 'non-recurring' charges: 5.6 million euros in 2024, 8.9 million in 2025 and 4.3 million in the first half of 2026 (acquisition, redundancy and restructuring costs); we treated them as ordinary costs. Goodwill is 96.3 million euros, 1.4 times equity. The pension provision is 0.3 million euros; off-balance-sheet guarantees are 0.25 million euros. There is no stock option plan.
en.latest: 22 October 2026: The company reported third-quarter results: revenue 100.2 million euros (organic growth 16.6%), EBITDA 12.0 million euros (margin 12.0%). Nine-month revenue was 287.9 million euros and EBITDA 34.5 million euros. The 2026 targets were kept. First half (report of 31 July 2026): revenue 187.7 million euros (+6.8%; organic +12.6%), net profit attributable to the group 11.2 million euros (8.8 million a year earlier), earnings per share 1.18 euros (0.94). That profit includes 2.2 million euros of financial income from remeasuring the commitment to buy out minority stakes.
risks: Debt is rising: net debt as reported by the company went from 28.2 million euros to 60.5 million euros in six months; nearly all profit is paid out as dividends while acquisitions are made with debt.

About a quarter of revenue comes from European institutions (first half of 2026: 24%; our calculation); this work depends on tenders and fell from 51.9 million euros to 45.4 million euros in the first half.

The company is based in Luxembourg and does most of its business in Switzerland and the United Kingdom. The inflation adjustment here uses French inflation; the franc and sterling exchange rates affect profit in euros.
